Tree

✓

A hierarchy of folders, projects or types. Each branch folds, and a click on a name shows its note.

starter.html, data-g="tree"

Example
  • src/
    • Orchestrator.Kernel/
      • Events/
      • Ports/
    • Orchestrator.Features/
      • Sessions/
      • Lifecycle/
    • Orchestrator.Web/
Variants
Large tree with states: 24 nodes, 4 levels
decidedopengap
  • src/
    • Orchestrator.Kernel/
      • Events/
      • Ports/
      • Projections/
      • Clock/
    • Orchestrator.Features/
      • Sessions/
        • Create/
        • Archive/
        • Registry/
      • Lifecycle/
        • StateMachine/
        • StateCheck/
      • Messages/
        • Inbox/
        • Delivery/
      • Workflows/
      • Templates/
    • Orchestrator.Store/
      • Notion/
      • Files/
    • Orchestrator.Web/
    • Orchestrator.Tray/

Use when

  • Folders, projects, packages or type hierarchies
  • Any hierarchy deeper than 2 levels

Do not use when

  • Items with the same attributes: use a table
  • A flat list: use the foldable list
  • Steps in order: use the roadmap
Parts
PartClassValue
Box.tree-boxWhite, outline
Lineone nodeCode font 13, names only
Branch▾ ▸Folds on click
Noteunder the treeBody font 14, the description
PhoneShrink to 50%, then scroll
CodeHTML to copy
starter.html, data-g="tree"HTML
<div class="tree-box" data-g="tree">
      <ul class="tree">
        <li data-note="The source root."><span>src/</span>
          <ul>
            <li data-note="Events, ports and projections. No feature code."><span>Orchestrator.Kernel/</span>
              <ul>
                <li data-note="Append with an expected version. One write path."><span>Events/</span></li>
                <li data-note="One interface for each outside system."><span>Ports/</span></li>
              </ul></li>
            <li data-note="One folder for each slice."><span>Orchestrator.Features/</span>
              <ul>
                <li data-note="Registry, create, archive."><span>Sessions/</span></li>
                <li data-note="State machine and state check."><span>Lifecycle/</span></li>
              </ul></li>
            <li data-note="The web host."><span>Orchestrator.Web/</span></li>
          </ul></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
Full ruleFrom artifacts.md

artifacts.md, section "Tree"

  • Write the tree as ul.tree in a .tree-box. Each li holds <span>name</span>, a data-note and an optional child ul.
  • Use the same tree for each hierarchy, with or without state.
  • Tree lines show only the names. A description goes into the note, not at the right of the name.
  • State: only when the tree is about states. Set data-state (ok, warn, bad) on each li. A colored square shows before the name. Add a .legend above the tree.
  • The script draws one line for each node, with ├─ └─ lines. Each branch folds and opens on its own. A click on a name shows its note under the tree.
  • Lines never wrap. On a narrow screen the tree shrinks down to 50%, then scrolls.

Tree with states

✓

A tree about states: a colored square before each name, and a legend above the tree.

starter.html, data-g="tree-state"

Example
decidedopengap
  • Orchestrator.Features/
    • Sessions/
    • Lifecycle/
    • Messages/

Use when

  • A tree where the state of each node is the message

Do not use when

  • A tree with no states: use the plain tree
  • States of items with no hierarchy: use marks in a table
Parts
PartClassValue
Squaredata-stateok, warn or bad
Legend.legendAbove the tree
CodeHTML to copy
starter.html, data-g="tree-state"HTML
<div class="tree-box" data-g="tree-state">
      <div class="legend"><span><i style="--c:var(--ok)"></i>decided</span><span><i style="--c:var(--warn)"></i>open</span><span><i style="--c:var(--bad)"></i>gap</span></div>
      <ul class="tree">
        <li data-note="One folder for each slice."><span>Orchestrator.Features/</span>
          <ul>
            <li data-state="ok" data-note="Decided. Registry, create, archive."><span>Sessions/</span></li>
            <li data-state="bad" data-note="Gap. The state machine and the state check live in two places."><span>Lifecycle/</span></li>
            <li data-state="warn" data-note="Open. Delivery waits for task K3."><span>Messages/</span></li>
          </ul></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
Full ruleFrom artifacts.md

artifacts.md, section "Tree"

  • Write the tree as ul.tree in a .tree-box. Each li holds <span>name</span>, a data-note and an optional child ul.
  • Use the same tree for each hierarchy, with or without state.
  • Tree lines show only the names. A description goes into the note, not at the right of the name.
  • State: only when the tree is about states. Set data-state (ok, warn, bad) on each li. A colored square shows before the name. Add a .legend above the tree.
  • The script draws one line for each node, with ├─ └─ lines. Each branch folds and opens on its own. A click on a name shows its note under the tree.
  • Lines never wrap. On a narrow screen the tree shrinks down to 50%, then scrolls.

Call stack

✓

The calls of one code path, in order, in the code style.

starter.html, data-g="callstack"

Example
Call stack · orch post questionC#
PostQuestion()                        Cli/Post.cs:42
├─ Envelope.Create(kind, body)        Stream/Envelope.cs:18
├─ store.WriteBody(body)              Store/NotionStore.cs:77  → creates a Bodies row
│  └─ NotionTransport.Create()        Store/NotionTransport.cs:30
├─ store.Append(envelope)             Store/NotionStore.cs:95  → creates an Events row
│  ← EnvelopeId
└─ Supervisor.Nudge(to)               Supervisor/Nudge.cs:12   → wakes the receiver

Use when

  • How one request or command runs through the code
  • Where a value comes from or goes to

Do not use when

  • The structure of the code: use a tree or a diagram
  • Steps for a person to do: use a numbered list
Parts
PartClassValue
Block.cb, plain preDark, top bar "Call stack · path"
Lineone callCall, file and line, → effect
Return←On its own line
PhoneShrink to 50%, then scroll
CodeHTML to copy
starter.html, data-g="callstack"HTML
<div class="cb" data-g="callstack"><div class="bar-top"><span>Call stack · orch post question</span><span>C#</span></div><div class="scroll"><pre>PostQuestion()                        Cli/Post.cs:42
├─ Envelope.Create(kind, body)        Stream/Envelope.cs:18
├─ store.WriteBody(body)              Store/NotionStore.cs:77  → creates a Bodies row
│  └─ NotionTransport.Create()        Store/NotionTransport.cs:30
├─ store.Append(envelope)             Store/NotionStore.cs:95  → creates an Events row
│  ← EnvelopeId
└─ Supervisor.Nudge(to)               Supervisor/Nudge.cs:12   → wakes the receiver</pre></div></div>
Full ruleFrom artifacts.md

artifacts.md, section "Call stack"

  • Use a code block (.cb) with the top bar "Call stack · <path>" and a plain pre (no data-lang).
  • One line for each call: ├─ └─ │ lines, the call at the left, the file and line at the right, then "→ effect" when the call changes something.
  • Mark a return value with "←" on its own line.

Properties

✓

The fields and values of one item.

starter.html, data-g="props"

Example
FieldUmpire.Analyzers
Targetnetstandard2.0
OwnerEngine
Sourcesrc/Analyzers/

Use when

  • The facts of one package, file, service or setting

Do not use when

  • Several items with the same fields: use one table with a row for each item
Parts
PartClassValue
Table.twTwo columns
HeaderField, item nameBody font 13, bold
CodeHTML to copy
starter.html, data-g="props"HTML
<div class="tw" data-g="props"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Umpire.Analyzers</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Target</td><td><code>netstandard2.0</code></td></tr>
        <tr><td>Owner</td><td>Engine</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Source</td><td><code>src/Analyzers/</code></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table></div>
Full ruleFrom artifacts.md

artifacts.md, section "Properties of one item"

  • Use a two-column table: "Field" and the item name.
  • For several items with the same fields, use one normal table with a row for each item.
